messages:
Maria (CS): FYI Montclair just flagged a big p99 spike this morning after a marketing send. Customers seeing timeouts and slow responses. Their org id: montclair-prod.

Maria (CS): Key details from them: spike ~09:10-09:40 UTC, mostly /v1/chat/completions, model=rwd-13b-qat, seq len ~1.2k tokens for a subset of requests. They attached a couple of example request traces.

Oliver (Support): I grabbed their dashboard. p95 is up to 450ms, p99 jumps to 3.7s for that window. Error rate is low, it's latency tail. No auth/billing errors.

Sam (SRE): @Jin can you look at runtime logs for montclair tenant around 09:10? I suspect KV-cache churn or big sequences causing kernel stall.

Jin (Eng Runtime): Pulling logs now. Seeing some OOM-ish GC churn on a subset of serving nodes handling montclair. Not full process OOM, but memory pressure causing slow preemptive evictions -> long latencies. Sample snippet:

```
2026-03-12T09:12:04Z node-7 runtime WARN tenant=montclair token_seq=1184 kv_evictions=3 kernel_block_ms=1520
2026-03-12T09:12:05Z node-7 runtime INFO tenant=montclair batch_size=1 model=rwd-13b-qat latency_ms=3720
```

Jin (Eng Runtime): Also noticed a small group of client IPs from montclair are sending back-to-back long sequences, effectively single-request tiny batches which pushes these nodes into hotspot mode.

Maria (CS): Customer confirms they had two back-end workers storming with full transcripts after the send — likely the cause. They want a quick mitigation.

Sam (SRE): Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) apply per-tenant request concurrency cap (soft throttle) to smooth bursts, 2) route montclair traffic to machines with larger mem pool (if available), 3) temporarily pin them to rwd-7b-qat to reduce memory per request. Which do we want to try first?

Jin (Eng Runtime): Quickest low-risk is the concurrency cap + routing to high-mem pool. Pinning model helps but could change quality. I can add a tenant-level throttle rule: max_concurrent_requests=6 and burst_tokens=10.

Sam (SRE): Go for throttle + routing first. Jin, set throttle and add montclair to high-mem pool. I'll watch node metrics.

Jin (Eng Runtime): Done. Commands I ran (console action trace):

```
# applied via ops console
set-tenant-config --tenant montclair --key concurrency.max --value 6
set-tenant-config --tenant montclair --key concurrency.burst --value 10
route-tenant --tenant montclair --pool high-mem-rt --force
```

OpsBot: Action logged: tenant=montclair config_update by jin at 2026-03-12T09:28:12Z

Sam (SRE): After change, p99 dropped from 3.7s -> 980ms within ~4 minutes. p95 ~280ms. Observed fewer long kv_evictions in logs.

Maria (CS): Montclair confirms perceived latency improved for their users but they still report occasional 1.2s tails during peak. They asked if there's a permanent fix.

Jin (Eng Runtime): Root cause summary: bursty long-sequence single-request patterns caused KV cache pressure and increased kernel blocking on a subset of nodes (noisy tenant behavior). Short-term throttle smoothed the arrival pattern and routing to high-mem nodes reduced evictions.

Jin (Eng Runtime): Next steps: 1) recommend Montclair add client-side batching/backoff (we provided a sample), 2) schedule tenant reservation for peak windows (we can provision 2 reserved slots), 3) add an adaptive OOM heuristic in runtime to pre-evict less-critical KV entries for long sequences. I'll open an eng task for the heuristic.

Maria (CS): I shared our recommended client change: use the header `X-Redwood-Client-Id` + exponential backoff and split transcripts into 512-token chunks where feasible. Example curl to reproduce pattern:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: montclair" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-qat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<very long transcript>"}]}'
```

Oliver (Support): I added Montclair to our recommendations doc and offered a scheduled reservation during their next campaign. They accepted a 2-hour reserved slot for next send.

Sam (SRE): Created incident ticket SRE-2026-142 to track the runtime heuristic and monitoring rule: alert if tenant p99 > 2s AND kv_evictions > 5 in 5m.

Jin (Eng Runtime): WIP PR for heuristic: will implement a sliding score per-tenant based on recent seq-length histogram and evictions, and trigger softer preemptive cache eviction + prefer low-latency nodes.

Maria (CS): Montclair will test next campaign with our temp reservation and bump us if they still see tails.

Oliver (Support): Closing the thread for now but keeping SLO watch. Adding a follow-up in two weeks to verify no regressions. :thumbsup:
